_comment_charters_rubrics: Charters and rubrics are DENIED to agents by design. They encode your judgment, and an agent that can edit its own rubric will eventually edit it toward agreeableness. Change them yourself.
_comment_network: curl and wget are denied so the numerical probe cannot reach the network. Probes run on synthetic data or the local cache; a probe that quietly downloads a dataset is unreproducible and uncapped.
_comment_ingest: ingest/ is denied to agents so a curator cannot 'fix' a failing validator instead of fixing its card.
_comment_user_channels: focus.md, kb/concordance_user.jsonl and ledger/user_verdicts.jsonl are the three channels running FROM the user INTO the system. They are read-only to agents for the same reason as charters and rubrics, and for one more: an agent that can write to the verdict file can manufacture approval for its own past output, and an agent that can write to focus.md can decide what the user is interested in. Note that Write(//ledger/**) is allowed above and this line overrides it for one file -- deny wins. The verdict file is written only by ingest/log_verdict.py, which is a CLI you run, not a tool agents hold.
_comment_write_note: kb/** and ledger/** remain writable so agents can maintain the base concordance, the card index and the bridge ledger. The three denies above are surgical exceptions, not a change of stance.
_comment_log_verdict_subcommand: Denying Write on user_verdicts.jsonl is not sufficient on its own: Bash(python ingest/*.py:*) is allowed, so an agent could append to the file legitimately by running log_verdict.py itself and manufacture approval for its own past output. The 'log' SUBCOMMAND is therefore denied specifically. 'pending', 'show' and 'context' stay allowed -- weekly-synthesis needs 'context' to feed bridge-finder and project-architect, and neither of the other two writes anything. If you add a writing subcommand later, deny it here at the same time.
